builder: pyrxd.gravity.swap_state: NegotiatedTerms.to_dict / from_dict; pyrxd.gravity.htlc_covenant: build_htlc_covenant_{rxd,ft,nft} / holder_hash; pyrxd.btc_wallet.taproot: build_htlc / claim_leaf_script / refund_leaf_script; pyrxd.gravity.swap_coordinator: assert_timelock_margin
provenance: REFERENCE vectors produced by pyrxd from its own builders — pyrxd is the reference PRODUCER here, so this suite is a regression lock against silent drift, not an independent cross-check. NO mainnet-anchored vector (tracked follow-up). The swap stack these vectors describe is UNAUDITED: passing this suite means a second implementation agrees with pyrxd's bytes, NOT that the protocol is safe. The 32-byte preimage below is a fixed ASCII string, deliberately not CSPRNG output, so that no conformance file ever carries a value that could open a funded HTLC. Guarded by tests/test_htlc_handshake_conformance_vectors.py.

notes.hashlock: H = SHA256(p), SINGLE sha256, exactly 32 bytes. p itself is exactly 32 bytes and NEVER crosses the wire.
notes.dest_hashes: taker_dest_hash / maker_dest_hash are hash256 (double-SHA256) of the holder script, NOT of a pkh.
notes.timelock_ordering: t_rxd must exceed t_btc by the verifier's margin IN WALL CLOCK — each leg multiplied by ITS OWN chain's block interval. The maker holds the preimage p, LOCKS the Radiant leg and CLAIMS the BTC leg, so the leg it locks carries the LONGER refund (Herlihy, arXiv:1801.09515 §1). t_btc counts BITCOIN blocks (~600 s) and t_rxd counts RADIANT blocks (~300 s): comparing the raw counts is a unit conflation, and it is why schema /2 still published an unsafe ACCEPT vector (t_btc=20 / t_rxd=60 = 3.33 h against 5.0 h with a 6.0 h margin required). Schema /1 published the ordering INVERTED as well. See issues #482 and #567.
notes.t_rxd_unit: t_rxd MUST be BLOCKS. The Radiant covenant CSV has no SECONDS encoding.
notes.omitted_defaults: counter_chain/value_amount/eth_timeout_unix_s/credential_ref are emitted only when they differ from the BTC defaults; a reader MUST apply the defaults for absent keys.
notes.credential_ref_is_off_chain: credential_ref is NOT substituted into the covenant bytecode. btc-rxd-credential-gated and btc-rxd differ only by credential_ref and their covenant_scriptpubkey_hex is byte-IDENTICAL -- that equality is the EXPECTED result, asserted by test_credential_gating_does_not_change_the_covenant_spk, not an accident of the comparison. The gate is off-chain pre-fund policy (swap_coordinator.pre_btc_lock_gate); the covenant pays whoever produces the pinned holder script with p, credentialed or not. Do NOT treat the section-4 SPK byte-compare as binding this gate.
notes.genesis_ref_enforcement: ft/nft: only NON-EMPTINESS is checked at NegotiatedTerms construction (swap_state.py:339-341); the 36-byte length is enforced later, fail-closed, at holder_hash (htlc_covenant.py:194-195). rxd: a non-empty genesis_ref is accepted and silently ignored -- it round-trips through the wire form and changes no derived value.
notes.hex: bare lowercase, no 0x prefix; genesis_txid in derivation_params is DISPLAY byte order, the 36-byte wire ref is reversed-txid || vout LE32.
notes.schema_revision: /1 published the INVERTED ordering (accepted t_btc=60/t_rxd=20). /2 corrected the direction and left the UNITS conflated, so its only ACCEPT vector was still unsafe. /3 is judged in wall clock and each margin vector now carries rxd_block_interval_s, because the verdict depends on it. Every version bump here is semantically incompatible; a consumer pinned to an older schema cannot tell them apart from the version alone.

hashlock_vectors.why: OP_SIZE <0x20> OP_EQUALVERIFY on both legs' claim branches rejects any preimage that is not exactly 32 bytes; a builder MUST refuse it before broadcast.
Same pin. A non-32-byte p that still satisfies H would be skipped by the 32-byte-only scrape and strand the counterparty (fixed preimage-length theft vector).

margin_vectors.why: insufficient margin in WALL CLOCK: the maker's Radiant refund opens at 9.25 h (111 blk x 300s), but the taker's counter-leg refund opens at 3.33 h (20 blk x 600s) and the margin needs 6.00 h on top — a shortfall of 0.08 h (ESTIMATED). The two legs count DIFFERENT chains' blocks; a raw block-count comparison accepted this (#567).

The two legs count DIFFERENT chains' blocks; a raw block-count comparison accepted this (#567).

timelock ordering violated: t_rxd (20 blk) must exceed t_btc (60 blk) — the maker holds p and LOCKS the Radiant leg, so that leg carries the LONGER timeout (Herlihy 1801.09515 §1). The reverse lets the maker refund the covenant while p is still secret and then claim the counter leg.

timelock ordering violated: t_rxd (12 blk) must exceed t_btc (71 blk) — the maker holds p and LOCKS the Radiant leg, so that leg carries the LONGER timeout (Herlihy 1801.09515 §1). The reverse lets the maker refund the covenant while p is still secret and then claim the counter leg. NOTE: NegotiatedTerms' cheap same-unit construction guard does NOT fire on this pair — it only compares t_btc and t_rxd when they share a unit. A conforming implementation MUST run the normalising check and not just the construction guard. NOTE 2: the 71 is not 43200/600. A SECONDS relative timelock is quantised by BIP68 to 512-second units, so 43200 s locks for floor(43200/512)*512 = 43008 s — 71.68 counter-chain blocks, not 72. A verifier MUST price a SECONDS t_btc on BIP68's 512 s grid and not on its assumed block interval: the two disagree by up to one block interval in EITHER direction (measured at 600 s/block: 592 s of the taker's margin handed to the maker at t_btc=20992 s, and 504 s of honest margin refused at t_btc=17400 s).
